title: Trust or Escalate: LLM Judges with Provable Guarantees for Human Agreement

live_model.evidence: Sec 3.1: "and GPT-4-turbo (Achiam et al., 2023) as judges"; Table 3 row "No Selection" = 100% GPT-4-turbo composition, Coverage 100%, Guarantee-Success 0%.

prompt.note: Appendix shows qualitative judge-decision transcripts ("Chat Assistant Example" cases) but never prints the pairwise-judge system/instruction prompt itself.

claim.metric: guarantee success rate across 1000 calibration/test splits, standalone GPT-4-turbo ("No Selection"), ChatArena
claim.location: Table 3, row "No Selection" (100% GPT-4-turbo); exact per-split test size and raw agreement % are not cleanly separable from the extracted table text

data.source: Chatbot Arena user-assistant interactions (Zheng et al. 2023, publicly released); paper uses an unreleased 5.2k-instance subset "sampled by Li et al. (2024a)"; no code/prompt repository link found in this paper

notes: GPT-4-turbo is run as a standalone judge baseline ("No Selection"/Heuristic Selection rows) against the paper's proposed Cascaded Selective Evaluation method, a genuine live-run claim, but (1) the pairwise-judge prompt itself is never printed anywhere in the paper, only example transcripts of its outputs, and (2) the results tables extracted as dense runs of concatenated digits (a PDF-table-extraction artifact), so no single GPT-4-turbo value could be confidently isolated. Both gaps stack, so this is ineligible rather than "maybe".
